purpose: Define ⇔R as a candidate process-algebra operator expressing recursive co-validity with preserved transformation history.
positive_role: binds process terms through recursive history
supports local process closure without globalizing the relation

formal_seed.interpretation: A and B are recursively co-valid under a preserved residue path R within a restricted admissibility domain.
formal_seed.expanded_form: A ⇔R B := admissible(A, B, R) ∧ preserves_history(R) ∧ local_scope(R)
formal_seed.non_substitution_rule: A ⇔R B does not license unrestricted substitution of A for B.
formal_seed.history_rule: The path R is part of the relation and cannot be discarded without changing the meaning of the expression.

allowed_uses: Relating process aspects that are mutually required but not identical.
Expressing residue-preserving co-validity between symbolic structures.
Binding exclusion-generated distinction to continuation pressure.
Encoding local process closure where transformation history matters.
forbidden_uses: Using ⇔R to claim -1 = +1 in standard arithmetic.
Using ⇔R as a global metaphysical proof.

relation_type_distinctions.=: Strict equality; permits substitution where formal conditions allow.
relation_type_distinctions.⇔R: Residue-bound recursive co-validity with preserved path history.
